history.dynasty: Vijayanagara (Krishnadevaraya inscription); 11-storey gali gopuram built by Rajah Vasireddy Venkatadri Nayudu (1807-1809)
history.period: Legendary origin; Vijayanagara-era patronage; present east gopuram early 19th century
history.summary: The foot-of-the-hill shrine of Mangalagiri's three-temple Narasimha complex: legend holds Yudhishthira, eldest of the Pandavas, installed the chief image of Lakshmi Narasimha here. The temple was patronized by the Vijayanagara rulers (an inscription of Krishnadevaraya records his visit and grants), and its 153-ft, 11-storey east gopuram - one of South India's tallest - was built 1807-1809 by Rajah Vasireddy Venkatadri Nayudu of Amaravati; Kanchipuram architects are said to have corrected its lean by digging a tank opposite the tower. Related to seq 13 (which covers the hilltop Panakala Narasimha shrine of the same complex) but this file documents the distinct foot-of-the-hill shrine. Coordinates are the geocoded foot-temple POI.

name: Sri Lakshmi Narasimha Swamy Temple (foot of the hill)
town_description: Mangalagiri (the 'Auspicious Hill') is a temple town in Guntur district between Vijayawada and Guntur, famous for its three Narasimha shrines and its handloom cotton sarees. It lies on the Guntur-Vijayawada highway, about 12 km from Vijayawada.

travel.airport: Vijayawada International Airport, about 35 km away.
travel.railway: Vijayawada Junction, about 12-13 km away; Mangalagiri railway station is about 2 km away.
travel.road: On the Guntur-Vijayawada highway, about 15 km from Vijayawada and 23 km from Guntur; frequent buses and taxis from Vijayawada.

visitor_information.best_time: October to March for pleasant weather; Brahmotsavams in February/March draw the largest crowds.
visitor_information.opening_hours: Reported as 5:00 AM-12:30 PM and 4:00 PM-8:30 PM (verify: one source lists 5:00 AM-8:30 PM continuous). The hilltop Panakala shrine is open only until about 3 PM.
